entries.message: On iPhone and iPad, a New Tab button floats at the bottom of the sidebar beside the sidebar button, so a new tab is always a tap away.
Switching between Sub-Spaces that show the same pinned tab keeps its page on screen instead of leaving it blank, and with extensions pinned, the pinned tabs stay still as you switch.
Pages show their loading progress as a stronger fill in the address field, and the thin loading line along the top of the page on Mac is gone.
Browser windows on Mac resize much smaller, so two fit side by side on a laptop screen, and the pinned tabs keep their place in a short window.
Zooming a page out on iPhone and iPad fits it to the window instead of leaving a blank band down the side.

On iPhone Duo held upright, the page and Space controls move into the bar across the top, leaving the sidebar more room, and the controls that don't fit fold into a menu, Settings first. Back and Forward always show on iPhone and iPad, dimmed until there is somewhere to go.
On iPhone Duo held upright, the controls stay in the top bar while the keyboard is open.
